pages.heading: Month by month
pages.body: One good moment for every month, from January to November. Some made the news. Some made us smile. All of them are ours.

pages.heading: A 15 year old from Tralee wins the Young Scientist
pages.body: The year opened with a teenager from Tralee taking the Stripe Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition. Her project, GlioScope, uses AI to spot brain tumour mutations from MRI scans, so doctors can avoid invasive sampling. Almost 2,000 entries came in and 550 reached final judging. She wins 7,500 euro and a trip to Kiel for the EU contest. Fourth year, and already ahead of us.

pages.heading: Ben Lynch skis into an Olympic final
pages.body: Ireland is not famous for ski slopes, so this one felt special. On 20 February, Ben Lynch, 23, finished eighth in the halfpipe final at the Winter Olympics in Livigno, with a score of 75.00. He was the first Irish skier to qualify for an Olympic final, and it was his Olympic debut. Jessie Buckley also won a BAFTA that month, but more on her next.

pages.heading: Jessie Buckley wins Best Actress at the Oscars
pages.body: On 15 March Jessie Buckley won the Oscar for Best Actress for Hamnet. The Irish Times called her Ireland's first ever best actress winner. Brenda Fricker won in 1990, but that was the supporting category, so this is a fresh first. Richard Baneham also collected a third Oscar that night, for visual effects. Not a bad evening for the home team.

pages.heading: Rory McIlroy wins the Masters again
pages.body: Rory McIlroy kept the Green Jacket. On Sunday 12 April he won the Masters for the second year in a row, finishing twelve under par after a closing round of 71 and beating Scottie Scheffler by one shot. It is his sixth major. The same month, Dermot Kennedy's album The Weight of the Woods landed at number one in Ireland, his third in a row.

pages.heading: Irish students win on the world stage
pages.body: Two prizes in one week. On 13 May, TU Dublin's SolHex, four third year Product Design students, won the NIBS Worldwide Business Plan Competition online finals with a habit support system called Daylight. Two days before, a Letterkenny Leaving Cert student was named European winner of the Earth Prize for Eco Purge, a plastic that helps break down microplastics.

pages.heading: Irish creatives take a top prize at Cannes Lions
pages.body: Ireland's ad people went to Cannes and came home with gold. Publicis Dublin won a Grand Prix for the strategy behind Heineken Ireland's The Pub That Refused To Die, Ireland's third ever. Better still for young talent, two junior creatives at TBWA Ireland won gold in Young Lions Print, with just 24 hours to make a water safety ad.

pages.heading: Mayo end a 75 year wait
pages.body: Seventy five years of waiting ended on 26 July. Mayo beat Kerry by one goal and twenty points to one goal and seventeen in the All-Ireland football final at Croke Park. They trailed by six in the 21st minute and led from the 37th. It is their fourth title and their first since 1951. Limerick won the hurling title a week earlier, on 19 July.

pages.heading: Mark English wins European gold in Birmingham
pages.body: On 13 August at the European Championships in Birmingham, Mark English won the 800m in 1:45.26, the first Irish man to win an individual European outdoor gold. Rhasidat Adeleke then took 200m silver in an Irish record of 22.28. Two days later Kate O'Connor won heptathlon gold with 6,751 points, another Irish record.

pages.heading: Katie Taylor says goodbye at Croke Park
pages.body: On 5 September, more than 80,000 people filled Croke Park to watch Katie Taylor beat France's Flora Pili on a unanimous decision. She retired as a three times undisputed world champion. Earlier that week, Met Éireann said the summer had provisionally been the warmest on record, at 16.28 degrees. A warm summer and a warm send off.

pages.heading: Fontaines D.C. go to number one
pages.body: Dublin band Fontaines D.C. reached number one with their fifth album, Dopamine Chamber, their second chart topper after Skinty Fia. It sold over 70,000 chart units in its first week, the third biggest opening week for an album in 2026. It also topped the Official Record Store Chart and the Official Vinyl Albums Chart.

pages.heading: Youth Night lights up clubs across the country
pages.body: On Friday 13 November, and the evenings either side, youth clubs and projects opened their doors for Oíche na hÓige. There were silent discos, drumming, art, coding, Lego robotics and virtual reality, plus podcasts and music made by young people. Minister Hildegarde Naughton visited Galway and said the atmosphere does not lie. In rugby, Ireland beat Argentina forty two to twelve.

pages.heading: December is already in the diary
pages.body: December has a few dates already confirmed. Dublin gets a week of film concerts at the RDS from 1 December. The Newgrange sun is due to be livestreamed on 21 December. Ireland's EU Presidency ends on 31 December, and Dublin sees in the new year with a three day festival. We will see you there.
bullets: 1 to 5 December: A Very Dublin Christmas, film concerts at the RDS (dublin.ie)
9 December: Christ Church Cathedral choir, 6pm (Discover Ireland)
21 December: Newgrange winter solstice livestream (Heritage Ireland)
30 December to 1 January: NYF Dublin (Visit Dublin)
31 December: Irish EU Presidency ends (Irish Presidency website)

pages.heading: Sport
pages.body: Big days at Croke Park, a big year for women's sport and a few firsts. We also remember Ciara Mageean, our European 1500m champion, who died on 1 November, aged 34.
pages.note: Mageean mention is in the divider body only. A full tribute page is for the tribute writer.

pages.heading: Katie Taylor says goodbye at Croke Park
pages.body: Around 80,000 people filled Croke Park for Katie Taylor's last fight. She beat Flora Pili of France by unanimous decision, with two judges scoring it one hundred points to ninety. Asked for something inspiring afterwards, she said "Let me just look around." She retired as a three time undisputed world champion. What a way to finish.

image.credit: Katie Taylor at the 2012 Olympics. Photo: cormac70 from London, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.author: cormac70 from London

pages.heading: Mayo end 75 years of waiting
pages.body: Seventy five years is a long time to wait for a cup. Mayo finally won the Sam Maguire on 26 July, beating Kerry by one goal and twenty points to one goal and seventeen. It is their fourth All-Ireland title. They fought back from seven points down, and Tommy Conroy kicked the last point. The cup is heading west.

image.credit: The Artane Band leads Mayo and Kerry around Croke Park before the 2026 final. Photo: Seankivlehan, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.author: Seankivlehan

pages.heading: Limerick lift the Liam MacCarthy again
pages.body: Limerick beat Galway in the All-Ireland hurling final at Croke Park on 19 July, one goal and twenty nine points to one goal and eighteen. They led by five at half time. Then Cathal O'Neill's goal in the 43rd minute, set up by Aaron Gillane, put the game out of reach. An eleven point win and a very happy Treaty county.

image.credit: The Liam MacCarthy Cup, photographed in 2011. Photo: Fti74, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.author: Fti74

pages.heading: Galway are ladies football champions at last
pages.body: Galway waited 22 years for this one. On 2 August they beat Kerry at Croke Park in the All-Ireland ladies football final, two goals and seven points to twelve points. Leanne Coen scored both goals and Eva Noone kicked the winning point late on. Kerry had a late effort ruled out, so it was nerves right to the whistle.

pages.heading: A record crowd for camogie
pages.body: A crowd of 33,419 came to Croke Park for the camogie final, a record for a camogie match played on its own. They saw Cork edge Galway by two goals and fourteen points to nineteen points. Saoirse McCarthy and Orlaith Cahalane scored second half goals, and the O'Duffy Cup went to Cork for a record 31st time.

image.credit: Croke Park, Dublin. Photo: Tolivero, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
image.author: Tolivero

pages.heading: Ireland women fill the Aviva
pages.body: A record 31,294 people watched Ireland women beat Scotland fifty four points to five at the Aviva Stadium, the first stand alone women's Test played there. Ireland scored eight tries and led forty seven to nil at half time. The win secured third place in the Six Nations and Ireland's first three win championship since 2020.

image.credit: Aviva Stadium, Dublin, at dusk. Photo: David Kernan, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.author: David Kernan

pages.heading: Triple Crown and a near miss
pages.body: Ireland won the Triple Crown, beating Scotland forty three to twenty one in Dublin on 14 March. Earlier they set a Twickenham record, scoring 42 points against England. The title slipped away when France beat England forty eight to forty six, with a Thomas Ramos penalty on the very last kick. Ireland finished second, and nobody would call that a bad year.

pages.heading: Birmingham: gold, silver and gold
pages.body: At the European Championships in Birmingham, Mark English won the 800m in 1:45.26, the first Irish man to win an individual European outdoor title. Twenty two minutes later Rhasidat Adeleke took 200m silver in an Irish record 22.28. Then Kate O'Connor won the heptathlon with an Irish record 6,751 points. Not a bad week at the office.

pages.heading: A big year for Troy Parrott
pages.body: On 19 April Troy Parrott won his first senior trophy, scoring and setting up a goal as AZ Alkmaar beat NEC five to one in the Dutch Cup final. Before that, Ireland led Czechia two to nil in a World Cup playoff but lost on penalties. Parrott told fans, "stick with us." In August he joined Real Betis for a reported 20 million euro.

pages.heading: Records and firsts
pages.body: Every year has a few moments that go in the trophy cabinet. Here are Ireland's records and firsts of 2026, from the stage to the stadium.

pages.heading: Records and firsts: everyday Ireland
bullets: Jessie Buckley became the first Irish woman to win the Best Actress Oscar, on 15 March.
Summer was provisionally the hottest on record, at 16.28 degrees. The old record was 16.19, set in 2025.
July was Dublin Airport's busiest month ever, with 3,839,635 passengers.
Wind power hit a record 3,898 megawatts on 14 February. Solar passed one gigawatt for the first time on 20 April.
A record 70,411 students got their Leaving Cert results in August.
Irish agri-food exports reached a record 20.8 billion euro for 2025.

pages.heading: Records and firsts: sport
bullets: Ireland scored a record 42 points and won by a record 21 at Twickenham, beating England on 21 February.
Ireland beat India at cricket for the first time in any format, by 34 runs at Stormont in June.
A record 31,294 watched Ireland women at the Aviva, the first stand alone women's Test there.
A record 33,419 watched the camogie final at Croke Park.
Mark English became the first Irish man to win an individual European outdoor title.
Rhasidat Adeleke (200m) and Kate O'Connor (heptathlon) both set Irish records in Birmingham.
Rory McIlroy won the Masters again, the fourth player to win it back to back.
